_comment: Lunar south-pole bases and their sun-tracking solar arrays (2026-10-27, CLAUDE.md 'Moon-base glints'; read by src/simulations/LunarBases.cpp).
EVERY size, layout, date and material below is a SCENARIO ASSUMPTION (the 2036+ setting: a fast expansion into space), to be tuned here.
Places: published candidate sites, approximate. Arrays: vertical panels on vertical-axis trackers following the Sun's azimuth (the Sun is within ~1.5 deg of the horizon at the pole).
lat/lon: selenographic (mean Earth / polar axis), east longitude. elev_m: above the 1737.4-km datum. horizon_dip_deg: how far below the horizontal the base sees (an elevated rim).

array: area_km2 at full build-out, split into `rows` trackers that appear in order between `online` and `complete` (UTC). row_tilt_sigma_deg / row_azimuth_sigma_deg: each row's tilt and tracking error (hashed, Gaussian). panel_flatness_deg: the slope error within a row (blurs the mirrored Sun). lean_deg: the panels' lean back from vertical. glass_f0: the cover glass' reflectance at normal incidence (Schlick).
sources: ILRS site: the Chang'e-7 target, a peak near the southeast ridge of Shackleton crater, ~88.8 S 123.4 E (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chang%27e_7; https://www.planetary.org/space-missions/change-7: the preferred candidate is Shackleton's rim). China's International Lunar Research Station is planned in the south-pole region (CNSA / Roscosmos ILRS guide, 2021: basic model by 2035).

Artemis base: the intersection of the Shackleton - de Gerlache connecting ridge with Shackleton's rim, 89.684 S 196.739 E (LROC image 'Traversing the Shackleton de Gerlache Ridge', https://lroc.im-ldi.com/images/1247; Glaser et al. 2014, 'Connecting Ridge - a landing site at the lunar south pole with extended illumination', https://elib.dlr.de/94242). NASA's Artemis III candidate regions (2022) include 'Connecting Ridge' and 'Peak near Shackleton'.
NASA power: Fission Surface Power (a 40-kWe reactor, NASA / DOE, 2022-) supplies most of it: the array is small (assumption).
Elevations: the Shackleton rim stands ~1.5-2 km above the datum in the LOLA heights (approximate).
